tags.description: Lose counters instead of taking damage
Recurring effects that make players sacrifice, destroy or otherwise remove permanents, usually creatures, every turn.
Abilities that can be activated from inside a graveyard.
Activated abilities that can be activated from your hand.
Cards with activated abilities. Not for cards that only gain or give activated abilities.
Spells with additional costs. See CR 118.8.
Cards that net you more than one mana at a time.
Counters that have no rules meaning, just aesthetic.

Affinity is an ability that reduces the mana cost of the spell by the number of permanents of a specified type that the player controls. Variations of this ability exist, such as referencing the number of cards in the players' graveyard or the number of attacking creatures.
Costs 1 less to cast for each instant or sorcery card in your graveyard
Cards that alliterate, either properly or per Treacherous Trapezist.
Cards that let you sacrifice permanents to play them for free/a reduced amount of mana
New ways for you to lose the game
New ways for you to win the game (or cause your opponent to lose)
Spells with alternative casting costs, which may be cheaper or more expensive than their mana costs. See CR 118.9.
Effects that turn things into creatures.
Noncreatures that can become creatures. For creatures that can stop being creatures, see [deanimate self](deanimate-self).
Your entire team gets +N/+N. Possibly limited to creature types or colors.
Cards that care about an artifact entering the battlefield.
Effects that turn things into artifacts.
Cards that care about attacking. See also [attacking matters-self](attacking-matters-self) for cards that care about themselves attacking.
Cards that care about themselves attacking. See also [attacking matters](attacking-matters) for cards that care about attacking in general.
Exile things as long as this permanent remains.
Effects which are iconically black.
Effects which are iconically blue.
Sacrifice something else to deal N damage. See also [fling](/tags/card/fling), [bombard-self](bombard-self).

Repeatable effects that, if an arbitrary amount of mana is dumped into them, will probably win you the game—for example, by drawing your whole deck, creating an arbitrarily large attacker, making an endless army of tokens, gaining infinite life, etc.
Returning a permanent from the battlefield to its owner's hand
Give an opponent something in exchange for a benefit to you.
A vehicle (or spacecraft) that comes with a built-in pilot to crew (or station) it.
Effects that deal damage, whether to creatures, players, or planeswalkers.
Cards that burn any target: players, creatures, battles, or planeswalkers.
Burn spells that have the mechanic of the set they debuted in.
Sometimes your own cards hurt you the most.

Card draw effects that can net you a bunch of cards at once. As a rule of thumb, to qualify for this tag, the card should let you draw at least three cards at a time and come out ahead by at least +1.
Cards that let you draw a card as they resolve or enter the battlefield.
Things that give you access to more cards.  (The technical meaning of card advantage can be much broader than this, but this is what we're using here.)
A collection of tags identifying properties and naming schemes in cards.
Mechanics that care about the cards in one or more graveyards.
Spells and abilities that let you cast spells as part of their resolution.
Cards that have a trigger when they are cast
Whenever you cast X, do something.
Cards you can cast or access from exile.
Cards you can cast or access from the graveyard.
Draw two cards, then discard a card.
Creatures that have their power determined by a characteristic-defining ability.
Creatures whose toughness is determined via a characteristic-defining ability.
Cards that have an ability that define something about it that would normally be found somewhere else on the card. Speicifcally, CDAs set color, types, subtypes, power, and/or toughness.
Modal spells where you pick one option out of three
The actual cost you pay for an effect (or for an alternate mode) will often be lower than the card's mana value.
Return a creature or permanent to the battlefield or to your hand at the moment it dies.
These creatures have only a class type, and no type correlating to whatever fantasy race they might belong to.
Cards that enter as copies of other things
Spells and abilities that care about the color(s) of mana spent on them.
Effects that can be used during combat to help a creature survive, destroy opposing creatures, or deal additional combat damage.
Modal spells where you pick two options out of four
Lands that will enter the battlefield tapped or untapped depending on certain conditions.
Dig through your library until you find a card meeting some criteria.
Consult effects that let you cast the card you find.
Consult effects that put the card you find onto the battlefield.
Effects that change control of cards, permanents, and spells.
Spells that do something equal to the number of colors spent to cast them.
Effects that copy things
"Brings back" a copy of a permanent card in a graveyard instead of the original. Could be a token copy, could be turning another card into a copy of it.
These cards can give you a copy of a legendary permanent you control that you can actually keep (instead of immediately sacrificing).
Effects that allow you to copy permanents of any type except for land.
Cards that make a copy of themselves
Make a copy of a spell on the stack.
Effects that copy specifically tokens, like populate.
Cards that allow you to bypass mana costs. This could be by making the spell free or by setting a static cost that's independent of the original.
Remove counters to do something.
Use any type of counter as fuel.
Cards that increase the amount of counters that would be given to something.
Spells that counter stuff. See child tags for variants on the behaviour; notably [counterspell-soft](/tags/card/counterspell-soft) which gives the opponent a buyout cost.
Cards that counter activated/triggered abilities. NOT for abilities that counter things.
For counterspelling that exiles the spell.
Counterspells that call out noncreatures specifically.
A "soft counterspell" gives the other player a chance to buy off the counter, such as with a mana payment.
Creature cards that generate additional creatures beefier than themselves. (Typically this means having a higher total power and toughness than the original creature.)
Cards that care about a creature entering the battlefield. Also known as Alliance in New Capenna.
Play lands from your graveyard.
Draw cards when dealing damage to an opponent
Cards that can give you some form of card advantage upon dealing damage, usually combat damage, to a player.
All the cycles from Magic history.
Cycles of lands that produce only colorless mana.
Dual land cycles. See also [dual land](https://tagger.scryfall.com/tags/card/dual-land) for non-cycle dual lands.
All the land cycles. See in particular: [monocolor land cycles](/tags/card/cycle-mono-land), [dual land cycles](/tags/card/cycle-dual-land), and [triland cycles](/tags/card/cycle-triland).
Monocolor land cycles.
The original cycle of shocklands from Ravnica block.
Things deal +N damage. See also [damage multiplier](/tags/card/damage-multiplier).
Things deal double or triple damage. See also [damage increaser](/tags/card/damage-increaser).
The "can't be blocked by power 2 or less" as named by WotC. See also [gives daunt](gives-daunt).
Typically black enchantments that come with a major drawback that could doom you. See also [lich effect](/tags/card/lich-effect).
Creatures that can stop being creatures. For noncreatures that may become creatures, see [animate self](animate-self).
Abilities that trigger from permanents being sent to a graveyard. See also [leaves trigger](leaves-battlefield-trigger).
Permanents with abilities that trigger when they die.
Create a triggered ability that may trigger later. Similar to a [reflexive trigger](reflexive-trigger).
Exiles cards from graveyard, but lets you cast copies of them. Essentially (usually) one-time recursion.
Cards featuring deprecated card types in some of their prints.
These cards were originally printed with the Legend creature type. Their type line read “Summon Legend” or “Creature — Legend”.
These cards want you to have multiple lands with different names.
Effects that give you two equally bad choices. Not to be confused with the action of "Dilemma".
Gets cards out of your opponent's hand and into their graveyard.
Ways to discard your own cards.
Put cards from the opponent's hand into exile, either permanently or by [banishing](banish-hand) them.
Cards that have a way to reduce their own cost
Cards that remove artifacts and/or enchantments.
Damaged creatures are exiled instead of dying.
Effects that give control of another card you control to another player
Effects that can create tokens under an opponents control.
2 MV "Destroy target creature, unless it's X"
Cards that represent a draft archetype in a given set. Typically designed as ten two-color uncommons (2CUDS).
Hurt a creature and gain life to match.
Hurt your opponent and gain life to match.
Spells and abilities that textually draw you cards. See also [pure draw](pure-draw).
Card draw effects that can net you additional cards repeatedly over time. Contrast [Burst Draw](burst-draw), which nets you multiple cards right away.
Cards that can hate on players drawing cards.
Effects that care about you drawing cards.
Cards that have some kind of disadvantage.
Effects that cause combat damage dealt to draw that many cards.
Artifacts that have to be sacrificed to do something.
Whenever you cast an enchantment spell, draw a card.
Effects that give a creature +N/+M. These values should be significant—usually at least +3/+3 or better, roundabouts.
Creatures that come with more creatures attached on ETB without reanimating them.
Cards that make things enter the battlefield untapped.
Creatures that are harder to block through keywords (flying, menace) or other means.
Cards that exile themselves once they've finished all their effects. Commonly seen on extra turn cards.
Cards which exile themselves (from the battlefield, from the graveyard, from your hand, etc.)
Exile something, but let them pay to get it back.

Effects that involve some amount of exponential growth. This can be an exponential value, or a token creation effect that would be exponential if allowed to progress unhindered. See [quadratic](quadratic) for a different, but similar kind of effect.

Effects that allow you to put additional lands from your hand, top of the library, or graveyard onto the battlefield outside of your normal once-per-turn land play. For effects that let you search your library for cards, refer to [tutor land](/tags/card/tutor-land).
Cards that grant extra turns.
Exile cards from a library. They're just gone now.
A card that is the primary, marquee legendary creature featured on the packaging of a pre-constructed Commander deck. It sets the main mechanical theme and color identity of the deck.
Cards that care about you controlling creatures with power 4 or greater.
Lands that sacrifice to tutor for other lands
Lands that take one mana and give you back another colour of mana, sometimes in greater quantities.
Reanimate or cheat something into play. If it would leave the battlefield, exile it instead.

Magic has various flavors of "vanilla", referencing cards with no abilities or only keyword abilities. For vanilla creatures (those with no abilities) see [is:vanilla](https://scryfall.com/search?q=is%3Avanilla) in Scryfall search.
Exile a card then return it to the battlefield (now or soon).
Flicker effects that work on all permanent types other than land.
Exile a card to be brought back after a set time (usually at end of turn).
Effects that can prevent all or most of the damage from an entire combat, similar to the card Fog. See also [pseudo-fog](https://tagger.scryfall.com/tags/card/pseudo-fog).
Fog effects where the damage prevention is or has the potential to be asymmetrical in some way, usually by exempting a subset of attackers/defenders.
Force an opponent to draw cards, whether they like it or not. The lesser used mode on Ancestral Recall.
Effects that care if you control creatures with a total power 8 or greater.
Cast other things without paying their mana cost.
Ways to sacrifice a permanent repeatedly that require no additional cost.
A permanent doesn't untap during its next N untap steps. For effects that prevent untapping indefinitely, see [lockdown](lockdown).
Prevent a creature from untapping for its next N untaps. For effects that prevent untapping indefinitely, see [lockdown](lockdown-creature).
These creatures, vehicles and spacecraft have only keyword abilities.
Cards with rulings where the rules manager is having fun with us. Not necessarily laugh-out-loud funny.
Lands that have you gain life when they enter the battlefield.
Effects that put creatures onto the battlefield from near the top of your library.
Combat tricks that give a creature +N/+N. See also [Enlarge](enlarge).
Cards that let you cast things from exile.
Allows you to play other cards from the graveyard.
Allows you to play other cards from zones other than your hand.
Granting the changeling ability doesn't actually do anything in the layer system, so these cards grant all creature types.
Cards that make a creature harder or impossible to block.
Cards that give a player a keyword ability, such as hexproof.

Cards that give +1/+1 counters. For permanents that only give +1/+1 counters to themselves, see [gains pp counters](gains-pp-counters) (which may overlap for cards that can give counters to themselves as well as others).
Put +1/+1 counters on all of your creatures.
See also [untapper-creature](untapper-creature).
Cards that require exiling other cards in graveyard as a cost for abilities and effects.
Exiles creatures from the graveyard for value
Effects which are iconically green
Cards that can be used to benefit other players, including opponents, usually by giving them resources
Cards that are able to deal damage or otherwise target multiple players at once.
Mess with your opponent's hand.
Cards that increase the maximum amount of cards you can hold.
Cards that hate on things — colors, card types, zones, etc.
Cards that specifically hate on cards with high power or toughness, typically at least 3-4.
Hate a specific card of your choice. Yes, that one.
Cards that "hate" on one or more mechanics in the set they were printed in.
Cards that make it harder for your opponents to target your stuff or punish them for doing so.
The more creatures your opponent controls, the more these cards scale up to punish them for it.
Effects that care about having no cards in hand.
Cards that exile other cards (or themselves) to use as reference marker for another effect.
Cards that care about the card types of other cards that they've exiled with a linked ability.
Look at the top N cards and put 1+ of them into your hand. Not to be confused with Red's pseudo-card-draw effect, [impulsive draw](/tags/card/impulsive-draw).

Cards which let you cast a card for a limited time off the top of a library (via exile). Use it or lose it. Typically a red card advantage mechanic. See also [impulsive mill](impulsive-mill). For the effect seen on the [card Impulse](/card/vis/34), see the [tag impulse](impulse).
Effects that last forever, sometimes tracked, sometimes untracked.
At/When/Whenever [event], if [clause], [effect].
A creature gains flying until end of turn.
Give your entire team a keyword.
A collection of all the keyword counters referenced by cards.
Specifically your land count, not [your opponent's](opponent-land-count-matters).
Ramp spells that net you more lands on your side of the battlefield.
Cards which reward you for playing lands.
Creatures that create one or more creature bodies when they die.
Cards that have triggers whenever a card (or cards) leave your graveyard
Double someone's life. See also [set life total](/tags/card/set-life-total) and [life divider](/tags/card/life-divider).
Get cards in exchange for your life (damage causes loss of life).
Cards that cost life to use; not necessarily with the "pay" keyword.
Cards that care about your life total being above or below a certain amount. This doesn’t include cards like Phyrexian Arena that simply want you to be alive.
Cards that cause you to gain life.
Equipments that attach themselves to a creature they create on ETB.
A permanent stays tapped. Named in the Color Pie 2017 article. See also [freeze](freeze).
Impulsive draw effects that let you play the exiled cards beyond this turn, letting you untap and have access to your full resources.
Draw a card, then discard a card. Mainly blue. See also [rummage](/tags/card/rummage), the red version, which discards then draws.
Effects that care about your things with mana value below some boundary value, usually 2 to 4.
Creatures that can bounce your opponent's stuff when they enter the battlefield.
Creatures which can repeatedly generate mana
Convert mana to other colors.
Cards that grow bigger when players cast spells.
Nonland cards that generate mana.
Noncreature artifacts that net increase your mana.
Cards with repeatable effects that you can dump a bunch of mana (at least 3) into each turn.
Effects that care about the amount, type, and/or qualities of mana spent to do a thing.
Cards that can be used to store mana for later phases and/or turns. The storing methods are varied—many use counters to count stored mana, while others create tokens.
Cards that can provide some amount of value without untapped lands.
Enters and causes all players to sacrifice a creature.
Creatures that scale in power and toughness with the number of lands you control.
Creatures that sacrifice themselves for benefit.
Shrink your opponent's whole board (or part of it).
Cards that have become memes in Magic, or are explicitly based off of memes.
A keyword action used in Magic to describe the action of a player taking cards from the top of their library and putting them into their graveyard.
Exile cards from the top of a library.
Cards that put cards from top of your own library to the graveyard. Check the tag "mill" for more.
Immediately gives you a small amount of mana or untapped lands back (typically no more than about one-third of the mana cost you paid)
Cards with names that imply something that card isn't, such as a mechanic or a color.
Spells which give you your choice from two or more distinct functions.
Spells where the modal options are: X, Mirror of X
Effects that care about at least one creature dying this turn.
The actual cost you pay for an effect (or for an alternate mode) will often be higher than the card's mana value. See also [cards with X in their mana cost](https://scryfall.com/search?q=m%3Ax).
An effect that filters cards at the top of the library, putting remainders into the graveyard.
This card represents multiple distinct identifiable characters on one face. Avoid using this for nameless mobs.
Land ramp that (potentially) nets two or more lands on your side of the battlefield
Removal for more than one, but less than all.  See also [spot removal](spot-removal) and [sweeper](sweeper).
Cards that interact with all of the players in the game. They might scale with the number of players or affect the turn order for example.
One-shot effects that put two or more creatures onto the battlefield on resolution.
These cards can target more than one object or player. Not mutually exclusive with [single target instant/sorcery](/tags/card/single-target-instant-sorcery).
Everyone sacrifices something.
Effects that care about card names: different names, same name, specific name, etc.
Spells (or, mostly spells) with names that identify them with a specific named character.
Cards that effectively "draw" from your opponent's library by exiling their cards and letting you play them.
Abilities that produce mana, but aren't mana abilities (as defined by CR 605.1)
Nonbasic lands that have basic land types.
Cards that care about creature types, but not necessarily on a creature card—so they're compatible with the Kindred cards from Lorwyn, for example.
Abilities with a mana cost outside the card's colors.
A creature deals damage equal to its power to another. Like Fight, but without the chance to fight back. See also [fling](/tags/card/fling) which involves sacrificing the creature.
Cards that make your opponents gain life.
Cards which create tokens which are one or more colours the original card isn't.
Cards that give you access to hidden information (Yours or other players)
Take a quick look at a players hand
Look at some number of cards from the top of libraries
Effects that scale positively with the number of players; i. e., "for each player", "for each opponent", etc.
Cards that involve phasing, whether the action or ability.
Cards that care about phasing, e.g. by seeing permanents phase in/out or by preventing phasing.
Cards whose activated abilities cost phyrexian mana
Effects that deal just 1-2 damage repeatedly.
Cards that let you play or cast the top card of your library. (Separate from [impulsive draw](https://tagger.scryfall.com/tags/card/impulsive-draw) which exiles it first.)
Sacrifice something else to draw cards.
Cards that provide power to all creatures you control. May be limited to certain types or colors.
Effects which care about the power of one creature (or multiple creatures individually, as opposed to as a total).
Effects which care about the total power of some set of creatures.
Cards that let you freely look at the top card of your library. You know, others don't.
Cards let you see the top card of your library and conditionally play it. See also [future sight engine](/tags/card/future-sight-engine) for an older variant in this vein.
Cards that prevent something from being sacrificed.
Effects that put +1/+1 counters on something when you gain life.
Effects relating to protecting your permanents (not necessarily via the protection keyword.)
Effects that give a form of protection to all permanents of a kind. (That may be hexproof, indestructible, protection, etc.)
Effects that can protect a creature, e.g. with protection,  hexproof, indestructible, etc.
Permanents with keywords or abilities that protect them from being interacted with on board.
Creatures that get bigger when you cast noncreature spells. For actual prowess, use kw:prowess. See also [prowess anthem](prowess-anthem).
Cards that do something very much like hexproof, but not hexproof.
Creatures with abilities that add incremental layers of growth.
Effects that sorta-proliferate some counters.
Effects that give you a choice of two damnations.
Names that are puns or otherwise a play on words
Spells and abilities that let you draw (a) card(s) without discarding other cards or sacrificing other permanents.
Abilities that instantly attach equipment and/or auras.
Non-Equip abilities that attach equipment.
Card names that are explicitly based on an existing quote.
A land that can net one or more mana of any color.
Effects that increase available mana for current or later turns.

Card names that match real world english animal names. "Manta ray" is accepted, while "Hurr jackal" is not. Adjectives can disqualify a card unless it is a part of their name. "Giant ladybug" is a species name and therefore accepted, while "Venomous dragonfly" is not.
Return permanent cards from the graveyard to the battlefield.
Cast a permanent spell from a graveyard.
Return creature cards currently in the graveyard to the battlefield. Not to be confused with [cheat death](/tags/card/cheat-death), which interacts right as the creature dies.
Reanimate from any graveyard.
Cards that specifically have the ability to reanimate cards opponents have, if not any card
These cards can return themselves to the battlefield if they're sitting in the graveyard. Not to be confused with [cheat death-self](cheat-death-self), where the card returns immediately after dying.
Get stuff back from your graveyard to use it again. See: reanimate (to battlefield), regrowth (to hand), and restock (to library).

Brings itself or other cards you own back from exile, regardless of what effect might have put them there. For effects that do this to your opponent's cards, see [processing](https://tagger.scryfall.com/tags/card/processing).
Effects which are iconically red.
An ability that triggers based on actions taken earlier during a spell or ability's resolution.
Immediately get mana or untapped lands back.
Effects that return other cards from your graveyard to your hand.
Effects that put an artifact back in your hand from the graveyard.
Return a creature from the graveyard to the hand
Effects that put an instant back in your hand from the graveyard.
Cards that can return themselves from the graveyard to the hand.
Effects that put a sorcery back in your hand from the graveyard.
Get things off the table.
Removal that can kill creatures by reducing their toughness to 0 or less.
Remove counters from stuff.
Remove counters from your permanents or yourself.
Cards that remove spells from the stack without countering them.
Exile this card from your graveyard: Do a thing. Doesn't need to be the specific Renew keyword, just cards that have an ability to exile themselves in the graveyard.
Things that give you access to more cards, repeatably.
Repeatable ways to create creature tokens
Repeatable ways to commit crimes by targeting an opponent or something they control.
Draw cards repeatedly, no matter if you go up on cards or not.
Repeatable ways to create noncreature tokens
Repeatable ways of putting +1/+1 counters on creatures.
Repeatable ways to draw a card with no additional cost or sacrifice, such as discarding a card
Repeatedly sacrifice stuff.
See also: [repeatable scry](repeatable-scry).
Repeatable ways to create tokens
Bounce something you control.
Bounce a land you control back to your hand.
Effects that return cards from the graveyard to the library. (Named in Maro's color pie 2017 article.)
Return any cards to your library from the graveyard, not caring about their types.
Cards that restock themselves.
Put cards from your graveyard on the bottom of your library.
Put cards from your graveyard on top of your library.
Cards that can only attack in specific circumstances.
Mana that has restrictions on what you can or cannot use it on.
Makes players reveal their hands more permanently than [peek](peek-hand)
Effects that opponents can buy off if they pay mana.
Discard a card, then draw a card. Mainly red. See also [loot](/tags/card/loot), the blue version, which draws then discards.
Effects that trigger when you deal damage to an opponent.
Permanents that have abilities that make them sacrifice themselves.
Effects that scale with how much damage a creature deals.
Effects which scale with the power of one or more creatures.
Cards that care when the player casting or controlling them casts their second spell for the turn.
Group Hug cards that benefit only certain opponents in particular.
A resolving spell or ability partially or completely replacing one of its own effects.
Your life total becomes N. See also [life divider](/tags/card/life-divider) and [life doubler](/tags/card/life-doubler).
Effects that give an arbitrary amount of +1/+1 until end of turn. See also [firebreathing](firebeathing) in red and [armoring](armoring) in white.
Set creatures' power/toughness, not necessarily a nerf. See also [humble](/tags/card/humble).
Something on the battlefield becomes a copy of something else.
Put counters on stuff based on other counters on other permanents.
Lands which enter tapped unless you pay two life.
Nerf a creature's power, temporarily or otherwise. Not to be confused with [humble](humble).
Prevent opponents from casting spells, and possibly also activate abilities.
Cards named with a single word in English. This may be a compound word.

Instant/sorcery spells that may target only one target. This is materially important for some effects that care about single targets. Not mutually exclusive with [multiple targets](/tags/card/multiple-targets).
Put a permanent from your hand onto the battlefield. (With or without a requirement to sacrifice it later.) Not related to the Sneak keyword first seen in TMT.
Cards that let you put lands on the battlefield from your hand without playing them.
Creatures entering the battlefield causes you to gain N life.
Removal for one target specifically.  See also [sweeper](sweeper) and [multi removal](multi-removal).
A common card design that is related to one or more of the main mechanics in a set
Cards that are particularly effective when you start the game with them.
Cards that require paying an additional cost per additional target.
Artifacts enter with a charge counter for each color of mana spent to cast them; creatures enter with +1/+1 counters.
Put +1/+1 counters equal to the amount of life gained.
Put a +1/+1 counter on each of up to N target creatures.
Cards that let you look at the top # cards of your library and put some into the graveyard.
Sorry I messed up your stuff. Here's a thing in exchange. (See also [humble](/tags/card/humble).)
_o\ Destroy all the things! See also [spot removal](spot-removal) and [multi removal](multi-removal).
Sweepers that are, or have high potential to be, one-sided.
Cards that affect the whole battlefield/all players in symmetrical, equal manner.
You might also be interested in [synergy-equipment](synergy-equipment) and [synergy-artifact-creature](synergy-artifact-creature).
Cards that have a scaling effect for each color on permanents or cards. See [synergy-color-every](synergy-color-every) for cards that care specifically about five-colored cards.
Cards that care about casting spells from exile.
Tap a creature to pay for/activate an effect
Cards that allow you to tap another permanent as part of an ability cost.
Non-basic lands which come into play tapped
Tap down permanents. For cards that tap stuff as a cost, see [tap outlet](tap-outlet).
Extract resources from your opponents when they try to do stuff, either by making them spend extra resources or by generating them for yourself.
Effects that let you steal cards and resources from your opponent.
Abilities that trigger when something (other than itself) enters the battlefield
Opponent reveals their hand, and you choose a card for them to discard.
Gain control of a permanent until end of turn. For continuous theft see [theft-creature](/tags/card/theft-creature).
Cards that care about you having seven or more cards in your graveyard.
Effects that check how many times they've resolved and do something different based on the result.
An ability that triggers on both entering the battlefield and attacking, similar to the Titan cycle from M11
Cards that completely replace the tokens that will be created with other tokens.
Generate resources from your opponent's actions without them being able to pay it off.

Providing incremental card advantage over time (usually by tapping to draw cards, although there are variants that [tutor](tutor), [impulsive draw](impulsive-draw), etc.) has been a staple effect for noncreature artifacts since the printing of Jayemdae Tome in Alpha.
A family of two-card rummage spells.
Abilities that trigger from inside the graveyard.
Instants that give +N/+0 to all your (attacking) creatures until end of turn.
Effects that put a spell or permanent into its owner's library.
Cards that directly search for a card from your library, and sometimes other locations as well.
Cards that tutor artifact cards.
Cards that tutor Equipment cards.
Cards that tutor noncreature artifact cards.
Cards that tutor creature cards.
Cards that tutor enchantment cards.
Cards that tutor Aura cards.
Cards that tutor cards from an opponent's library.
Cards that tutor land cards.
Tutors with restricted effects that are able to search for any land.
Cards that tutor basic land cards.
Cards that tutor basic Mountain land cards.
Cards that tutor basic Plains land cards.
Cards that tutor legendary cards.
Cards that tutor cards with a certain mana value.
Tutor to specific zones.
Cards that tutor something out of the library and straight onto the battlefield.
Cards that tutor into exile for later use.
Cards that tutor cards to the player's hand.
These cards are tutored by another specifically by their name. For the cards that tutor them, see [tutors by name](tutors-by-name).
These cards tutor other cards by their name. For their tutor targets, see [tutored by name](tutored-by-name).
"Typal" cards that exclude one or more creature types rather then including a few. Usually to prevent loops, have a specific typal limitation, or to prevent changelings from joining in.
Also known as the "Federation" mechanic in TRK.
Gained the Noble type, either after it was reintroduced with the big sweep at Eldraine launch, or at a later date.
Cards that were printed with a type-line that has since been updated. For cards whose token generation has changed, see [Token Errata](token-errata).
Cards that received a new type because it fit them, or because they were lacking one before.
Effects that trigger when something becomes tapped. For cards that care about tapped permanents, see [synergy-tapped](synergy-tapped) and [tapped matters-self](tapped-matters-self).
Creatures with one or more single creature types that are unique to them, not counting creature types on tokens.
Cards with a power/toughness not seen on any other card.
No other card has this same type line. Acorn, playtest, and rebalanced cards may count as unique, but they don't make non-acorn, non-playtest, non-rebalanced cards stop counting as unique.
Spells or abilities that require tracking events without explicitly noting them. See also [noted tracked information](noted-tracked-information).
Cards that can untap things.
Effects that last forever but aren't tracked by anything. For these purposes we're not counting ETB clones.
Mana rocks that do extra things.
Creatures and vehicles that are french vanilla (having only keyword abilities) after entering the battlefield. They may have "enters the battlefield" or "on cast" trigger.
These creatures are effectively just vanilla after entering the battlefield. They may have an enters-the-battlefield or on-cast trigger.
Cards that care about the number of colors among permanents you control.
Collection tag for the Ward keyword. Should be 1:1 with kw:ward.
This creature's P/T is equal to the number of creatures you control. Named in the Color Pie 2017 article.
Cards that have reduced use in formats that do not allow more than one card with the same name to be used, such as in Commander or Highlander.
Effects which are iconically white.
Effects which allow you to bring in cards from outside the game.
Cards that don't explicitly care about the value of the {X} in their costs (usually because [mana spent matters](mana-spent-matters) in some other way).
Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell, create a creature token.
